scenes.question: Which dots belong to the same event?

beats.say: Look at a school playground from above. Children stand in little groups. You can spot each group because its members stand close together. But if you overlay photos from a whole week, all the groups blur into one big crowd.

Fire detections are the same. Points close together in space and time usually belong to one burning event or one site. Formula forty-one, DBSCAN clustering in space and time, groups them without being told how many groups to expect, and a time window stops different days from merging into one giant cluster.

parts.say: N epsilon of p is the neighbourhood of a point p: all the points q within a distance epsilon s of it, measured in kilometres with the haversine formula.
And, this is the key addition, also within a time window, epsilon t days. Two fields side by side, burned a week apart, are no longer neighbours.

A point is a core point if its neighbourhood holds at least minPts points; FIREWORK uses three. Clusters grow outward from core points. Points that belong to no cluster are called noise. Remember, a cluster is a grouping for analysis, not a count of fires.

steps.label: Detections
steps.say: Take all S-NPP detections in Punjab and Haryana in October and November 2023: 34,383 points. Each point is one detection, a pixel, not a fire.

steps.label: Clusters, space only
steps.say: Cluster by space only, within 1.5 kilometres, and we get 945 clusters. But the largest swallows 19,962 points: a chain across the whole farm belt.

steps.label: Clusters, space and time
steps.say: Add a window of one day either way, and we get 2,812 clusters, with a median of 4 points and a largest of 880. And 47 percent of points are isolated. Now the clusters look like real, separate events.

beats.say: These are S-NPP detections near Ludhiana, in October and November 2023. On the left, space-only clustering merges neighbouring fields burned on different days into one large cluster.
On the right, with a window of one day either way, the clusters split into separate events. Grey points are noise. Each coloured group is now one burning event, close in both place and time.

beats.label: Sites on the globe
beats.say: On the FIREWORK website, open the Sources page. Clusters turn thousands of points into a manageable number of events and sites.

beats.label: Hot pixels by ground type
beats.say: That matters because persistence and night share are properties of sites, not of single pixels. The distance window is set per sensor, because their geolocation differs.

points: Neighbours: close in space AND within ε_t days
Core points with ≥ minPts neighbours grow clusters
Space + time: 2,812 clusters instead of one giant chain

beats.say: So, to remember: group points that are close in both space and time, and let the clusters form by themselves. Without the time window, a whole farm belt becomes one blob.
